newsitem.title: USA: Wis. voters approved $295.9 mln school borrowing.
newsitem.headline: Wis. voters approved $295.9 mln school borrowing.

text.p: Wisconsin voters approved $295.9 million of school district borrowing through April and could back as much as $620 million more before the end of the year, according to a Wisconsin Taxpayers Alliance report released this week.

The 1997 numbers reflect increasing borrowing by school districts in Wisconsin since the 1994 education funding reform measures approved by the legislature, the alliance reported in its Focus publication Monday.
School districts ran 71 successful ballot issues totalling $403.3 million in 1995 and 83 successful questions in 1996 for $663.2 million, the alliance said.
And in the first four months of 1997, voters in 28 school districts approved 38 ballot questions for $295.9 million of authorized issuance, the alliance said.
Another $613.6 million of building borrowing and $6.1 million for operating expenses could go before voters this year as well, the alliance said.

The elections allow districts to increase property tax levies above cap limits, which also leads to a required increase in the state aid to the districts, leading to a government "sale" on education, the alliance said.
